## Purpose Decode rows in the bf16 sparse MLA path go through the ragged **prefill** kernel, whose grid is `(q_len, heads_blocks)`. GLM-5.3-Flash at TP8 has one head block, so during decode with concurrency 4 launches only 4 workgroups on 256 CUs. Clearly underutilized. commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Accept successful 2xx responses for batch output uploads
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Batch result uploads treat successful HTTP 201/204 responses as failures, upload the same output five times, then raise. Accept 2xx responses in both memory and file upload paths.

## Claims

- Successful PUT responses complete after one upload, without retry sleeps.
- Error responses retain the existing retry count and response-body diagnostics.

## Validation

A focused harness loads upload_data directly from the checked-out source by AST extraction against a real local aiohttp PUT server, with real file and request-body I/O. Only retry sleep is replaced.

Before: HTTP 201/204 each caused five PUTs and an exception, in both upload paths.
After: 10/10 HTTP cases passed: 200/201/204 succeed once, 400/500 retain five attempts and error details, each from memory and file. Seven exact-source unit cases also pass under AST isolation.

Local workspace-only harness command (the harness is not included in this PR): `.venv/Scripts/python.exe ../validate_batch_upload.py`.

This does not claim a full run-batch engine run or native pytest pass. Native test collection requires the unavailable vLLM runtime dependencies.

Native regression command for a fully installed development environment (not yet passed locally): `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/launchers/test_run_batch.py -k upload_data -q`.

Ruff 0.14.0 check/format, git diff --check, and applicable pre-commit hooks (including mypy 3.10/3.12 and test/CI tethering) pass. Windows required UTF-8 mode and Git Bash in PATH. The unrelated Dockerfile graph updater was skipped; no Dockerfile changed. Existing Buildkite benchmark and entrypoints launchers suites include these test files.

## Details

The existing success condition accepted only status 200. RFC 9110 section 9.3.4 defines successful PUT responses including 201 and 204: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html#section-9.3.4 . Azure Put Blob returns 201: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/rest/api/storageservices/put-blob .

Duplicate checks: open PR searches for upload_data, upload 204, 2xx, and upload batch found no matching fix. AI assistance: Codex assisted analysis, implementation, and validation.

commits.pr_title: [BugFix] Pick the DP world-group port at bind time via the coordination store
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

With `--data-parallel-size N`, the DP world group's rendezvous port comes from `_data_parallel_master_port_list` — probed once at config time and consumed by `get_next_dp_init_port()` when the engines finally call `init_process_group`, **minutes later** (after worker spawn, CUDA init, and model load). Nothing holds the port in between, so any other process — most commonly a sibling vLLM instance cold-starting on the same host, the standard shape in RL rollout fleets — can take it. Startup then fails at its very last step with the engines hanging on:

```
(Worker pid=...) torch.distributed.DistNetworkError: The server socket has failed to
listen on any local network address. port: <n>, ... EADDRINUSE
```

#36330 fixed exactly this defect for the elastic-EP stateless groups: rank 0 binds an ephemeral port, keeps the listening socket, and publishes the port through a coordination TCPStore. This PR extends that mechanism to the last remaining pre-allocated consumer, the world group:

- `launch_core_engines()` creates the coordination store for online DP (dp>1, engine rank 0 local; the initial MoE-only gate was removed in a follow-up commit, see below) when none exists yet, and hands its port to engines through the existing startup handshake (`_coord_store_port`).
- `init_distributed_environment()`: for the DP path, group rank 0 creates the world-group TCPStore on port 0 — the kernel assigns the port and the store owns it from birth — then publishes the resulting port via the coordination store; other ranks read it and connect. All ranks pass the store to `init_process_group` (`store=` argument), so the port is never released between choice and use. Without a coord store the previous behavior is unchanged.

## Design notes for reviewers

Answers to the questions this diff naturally raises.

**Why publish through a TCPStore rather than the handshake or spawn args.** The port does not exist until group rank 0 binds — after every engine has spawned and after the handshake replies have gone out (the frontend replies to each HELLO as it arrives; rank 0 has not bound yet at that point). Delivery therefore needs a channel that (a) works after all startup messages, (b) blocks until the value appears (ranks reach group init in arbitrary order), and (c) is reachable from both consumer levels: EngineCore processes (DP gloo group, store-based since #36330) and workers (world group), which have no handshake connection to the frontend at all. A key-value store with blocking `get` is the smallest thing satisfying all three, and #36330 already built it — this PR only extends where it is created (MP path, before the Ray branch) and adds one consumer.

**Why rank 0 creates the store on port 0 and reads the port back.** Ownership must never gap: the world-group TCPStore itself binds port 0, owns the kernel-assigned port from birth, and `.port` reads it back for publication — the same readback pattern the coordination store (and zmq's `LAST_ENDPOINT`) already uses. The already-bound store is then passed to `init_process_group` via `store=`; torch requires `store` and `init_method` to be mutually exclusive, hence `init_method=None if world_pg_store else distributed_init_method` at both call sites. Rank 0 passes `wait_for_workers=False` because workers can only connect after the port is published, so the master cannot block for them inside its own constructor; PG init synchronizes through store keys as usual. An earlier revision of this PR bound a raw socket manually and handed it to `TCPStore(master_listen_fd=...)`; review simplified it to `TCPStore(port=0)` — same invariant, one layer less, and it drops the fd-adoption/libuv compat surface (cf. the `use_libuv=False` pin in `StatelessProcessGroup.create` for pytorch#150215).

**An externally-built store is equivalent to the torch-built one.** The constructor arguments mirror torch's own `_create_c10d_store` (`world_size`, `is_master=(rank == 0)`, group timeout, `multi_tenant=True`); both paths converge in `_new_process_group_helper`, which cannot tell who built the store. `store=` is the public contract torchelastic uses in production. Two known differences, both benign: (1) `wait_for_workers=False` on rank 0 (see above) moves a missing-worker failure from store-construction timeout to PG-init rendezvous timeout — the behavior torchelastic deployments already run with; (2) torch wraps rendezvous-built stores in `PrefixStore("default_pg")` but takes a passed store raw — harmless because the store is freshly created and dedicated to this group, and all members take the same branch.

**Store-creation guards.** Each condition excludes a deployment where creating the store would be useless or wrong: `dp_size > 1` (no consumer otherwise), `not offline_mode` (scope: offline keeps existing behavior), `dp_rank == 0 and local_engine_count > 0` (the store must bind on the DP master node; an API-server-only frontend would `bind()` an IP that is not its own), `not enable_elastic_ep` (the Ray actor manager creates its own store later, unchanged from #36330). An earlier idempotency check on `_coord_store_port` was dropped: no in-tree writer can set the field before this block runs.

**Fallback path is byte-for-byte the old behavior.** With `_coord_store_port` unset (offline, external launcher / SPMD, elastic, or an older frontend during version skew), `world_pg_store` stays `None` and both changed call sites degrade to their previous form.

**How the store address travels.** One field added to the existing handshake copy-list covers remote (headless) MP engines; local engines receive it in the config at spawn, Ray actors in the actor-constructor config, and workers inherit it when the executor spawns them. Non-MoE MP engines are rewritten to independent dp=1 (`reconfigure_for_independent_dp_rank`) and never consume the store; the non-MoE case that needs it is the Ray DP backend (no such rewrite), which is covered via the actor-constructor config.

**Lifetimes.** The coordination store lives on the `launch_core_engines()` frame, which runs `wait_for_engine_startup()` after its yield — so it stays alive exactly until all engines are ready, then is discarded. The world group's own rendezvous TCPStore is a separate, process-lifetime object. The two are deliberately not merged: reusing the coordination store as the group's rendezvous store would make the frontend process a runtime dependency of every engine collective.

## Reproduction & A/B results

Hardware: single GB200 node (aarch64, 4 GPUs), image `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` (2026-08-04). Arm "fixed" = same image with this patch applied. Model: a 9-layer MoE test checkpoint with dummy weights (`--load-format dummy`); any small MoE reproduces, e.g. `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite`.

Two experiments, all rounds on identical images/configs:

1. **Deterministic squatter**: start `vllm serve <moe> -dp 4 -tp 1` with `VLLM_PORT` set (making the config-time probe deterministic); a squatter process waits until the EngineCore processes exist (probe done, world-group bind not yet) and then binds-and-holds `[VLLM_PORT, VLLM_PORT+16)`:

   ```python
   # squat.py — run alongside the server, after EngineCore appears in its log
   import socket, time
   socks = []
   for p in range(42000, 42016):
       s = socket.socket(); s.bind(("0.0.0.0", p)); s.listen(); socks.append(s)
   time.sleep(600)
   ```

2. **Concurrent cold start (RL shape, no artificial interference)**: two `-dp 2 -tp 1` instances on one node, same `VLLM_PORT`, started simultaneously.

| experiment | main | with this fix |
|---|---|---|
| squatter | **6/6 startup failure** (EADDRINUSE at world-group init, process hangs) | **8/8 healthy** (full band squatted) |
| concurrent cold start | **6/6 startup failure** | **6/6 healthy** (both instances) |

The failure mode on main matches field reports: the server does not exit — it hangs after minutes of model loading, which is the expensive way to fail.

## Relationship to existing work

- **#36330** (merged) introduced the coordination-store mechanism and fixed the stateless-group half of this defect; this PR completes the class by migrating the world group. Same defect statement, same cure.
- Related symptom reports: #39015 (EADDRINUSE on 29500-family defaults), #28498 (port-conflict tracker), #14919.
- Sibling PRs for other port-race sites: #50960 (zmq shm broadcast, merged), #50965 (`get_open_port` reserved-range livelock, merged), #50969 (Ray executor TCPStore host), #50999 (single-node executor `file://` rendezvous).
- Duplicate-work check: [open PRs touching dp master port](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+data_parallel_master_port), [open PRs mentioning 39015](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+39015+in%3Abody) — none migrate the world group to the coordination store.

## Test Plan

```
pytest tests/v1/engine/test_dp_world_group_port.py tests/v1/engine/test_core_engine_actor_manager.py -k "world_group or coordination_store"
```

- A/B experiments above (deterministic + statistical, 26 rounds total, zero exceptions).
- Existing DP suites (`tests/v1/test_async_llm_dp.py`, distributed tests) exercise the changed init path end to end; behavior without a coord store is unchanged by construction.

## Test Result

- See table above; `pre-commit` clean on the changed files (the forbidden-import hook's `pickle` flag on `parallel_state.py` is its pre-existing allowlisted import surfacing under a worktree path prefix).

## AI Disclosure

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for investigation, implementation, the A/B experiments, and drafting this description. Opened as a draft for the submitter's final line-by-line review before requesting maintainer review.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)


## Reproduced nightly A/B (2026-08-07)

Actual run: `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` on h200-0 (baseline, image `sha256:40e504de…`) and h200-1 (PR head, image `sha256:928dde7d…`), each with 8× H200. The repro calls `init_distributed_environment()` with the same coordinated-online-DP branch this PR changes. A squatter binds the exact port returned by the baseline `get_next_dp_init_port()` after its probe socket closes and before `init_process_group()` starts.

| base `24c939c47d` | `torch.distributed.DistNetworkError`: `EADDRINUSE` while TCPStore listens |
| PR head `ad4aec4ed` | passes: rank 0 binds `:0`, creates the TCPStore from that held socket, then initializes the world group |

The base follows `tcp://<squatted-port>` and fails; the head uses `_coord_store_port` and succeeds. This is deterministic rather than a timing-only cold-start test.

## Non-MoE DP completion (2026-08-07)

The original coordination-store creation was incorrectly gated on `model_config.is_moe`.  This misses ordinary replicated DP models: `init_distributed_environment()` still creates the DP-expanded world group whenever `data_parallel_size > 1`, so it fell back to the pre-allocated `_data_parallel_master_port_list` and retained the exact probe-to-bind race.

PR head `ad4aec4ed` fails `AssertionError: non-MoE DP did not receive a coordination TCPStore`; commit `2827357fb7` passes on both hosts: `PASS non-MoE DP received a coordination TCPStore`.  The added focused pytest passes, and ruff, mypy-3.10, and full changed-file pre-commit pass.

The change removes only the MoE gate; all online local rank-0 DP launches now retain the coordination TCPStore until EngineCore startup, allowing rank 0 to bind-and-hold the actual world-group listener before publishing its port.

On h200-0, mounted the PR head into `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` and ran `vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --port 18018 --data-parallel-size 2 --data-parallel-size-local 2 --data-parallel-rpc-port 0 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.45 --enforce-eager` on two H200 GPUs. Both non-MoE DP EngineCores initialized, the API reached `GET /v1/models` (200), and `POST /v1/completions` returned a completion. This exercises the same non-MoE DP launch branch protected by commit `2827357fb7`.

## Fresh non-MoE nightly confirmation (2026-08-07)

After the follow-up commit `2827357fb7`, h200-1 re-ran production `launch_core_engines()` for non-MoE, MP DP=2 in `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` (head `sha256:928dde7d…`, `--gpus all --network host`). The current head printed `PASS non-MoE DP received a coordination TCPStore`. This confirms the rebase/current branch still covers the non-MoE variant that `ad4aec4ed` initially omitted.

## port=0 simplification validation (2026-08-08)

Commit `613d35eacf` replaces the manual socket bind/listen/detach + `TCPStore(master_listen_fd=...)` handoff with `TCPStore(port=0)` + `.port` readback (review suggestion). Validated by driving the real modified `init_distributed_environment()` in two spawned processes (dp=2 config with `_coord_store_port` set): rank 0 created the world-group store on a kernel-assigned port and published it, rank 1 read it from the coordination store and connected, `init_process_group(store=)` formed the 2-rank world group, and a gloo `all_reduce` returned `[2.0, 2.0]` with clean exits. ruff check/format pass. The earlier GPU serving validation predates this commit; it should be repeated before undrafting.

## Test coverage (2026-10-06)

Two tests, both CPU-only (gloo), run as part of `pytest v1/engine`:

- `tests/v1/engine/test_dp_world_group_port.py`: two spawned processes bring up a DP=2 world group with the pre-allocated port already taken by another socket. With a coordination store the group binds its own port and both ranks all-reduce correctly; without one the pre-allocated path still works. Checked against unpatched `main`: the taken-port case fails with `EADDRINUSE` on the pre-allocated port, the fallback case passes. On this branch both pass (27 s).
- `test_coordination_store_held_only_by_the_online_dp_master` (rewritten from the earlier non-MoE test): a table over launch configurations. The online DP master holds a reachable store for both the mp and ray backends; non-master nodes, offline mode, elastic EP and single-engine deployments do not. Against unpatched `main` the two "holds a store" cases fail and the four "no store" cases pass.

## MI355 CI failure (build 93141) and fix (2026-10-07)

`:amd: (MI355) Distributed DP Extended` hung for 30 minutes in `test_async_llm_dp.py` with DP=2/TP=2 on both attempts, while the L4 run of the same step passed. In each attempt one worker of the DP-rank-1 engine never reached the world-group init: it was stuck on the coordination store (`wait timeout ... keys: /world_pg_port` in the retry), and its three peers then waited 30 minutes on its gloo key.

Root cause: `get_cached_tcp_store_client` caches one connected client per process. `DPEngineCoreProc` populates it in `_init_data_parallel` before it creates the executor, so with the default fork start method every worker inherited the same connected socket, and the two TP siblings of one engine interleaved their requests on it. The L4 run of the same step shows no spawn override either, so it forks as well; whether the interleaving corrupts the stream depends on whether the siblings' requests overlap, and that run did not hit it. The hazard is therefore not ROCm specific. This PR is the first to read the coordination store from workers at init, so the latent cache issue surfaced here.

Fix: the port exchange needs the store once per worker, so it now opens its own short-lived client instead of the process-wide cached one. The cached client itself is still not fork-safe for its other callers (elastic EP); that is pre-existing and left for a follow-up.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Keep MLA derived weights in place on weight reload
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

With CUDA graphs on, `sleep(level=2)` + `reload_weights` (or any in-place weight update) corrupts MLA output in two configurations: `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`, where output turns to garbage, and DCP query replication (`dcp_q_replicate`), where output degrades silently. The cause is the same in both. `MLAAttention.process_weights_after_loading` rebinds derived weights to new tensors: the AITER BMM weights `W_K`/`W_K_scale`/`W_V`/`W_V_scale`, and the DCP gather `W_UK_T_dcp_qrep`. Captured graphs then keep reading the old storage. This PR copies them in place with `replace_parameter(..., prefer_copy=True)`, as the default branch already does for `W_UV`/`W_UK_T`.

## Claims

- Fixes both AITER BMM branches, FP8 (gfx942) and MXFP4 (gfx950), and DCP query replication. The DCP fix applies to every DCP-capable MLA backend.
- `test_reload_weights` now fails if any module's device tensor moves across a reload, and runs with AITER on ROCm. This catches this bug class generically, not just these four tensors.

## Validation

DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat, CUDA graphs, 2 cycles of level-1 full, level-1 selective, and level-2 + `reload_weights`:

| GPU (branch) | TP | Before | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| MI300X (FP8) | 1, 2 | garbage after level 2 (`" Paris.\ntopNavRename to topNavRename…"`); `W_K` address changes | sane on every wake; `W_K` address unchanged |
| MI355X (MXFP4) | 1, 2 | garbage after level 2, then `" Paris."` only | sane on every wake; `W_K` address unchanged |
| MI300X, TRITON_MLA, DCP 2 + `dcp_q_replicate` | 2 | all 8 outputs change after level 2 and stay changed (`"Paris, the capital city of France, Paris is the capital city of the the – well, you know."`); `W_UK_T_dcp_qrep` moves in all 27 layers on both ranks | matches pre-sleep output; nothing moves |

`enforce_eager` and `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP8BMM=0` were already unaffected.

`pytest tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_reload.py -k "test_reload_weights and DeepSeek"`: without the fix, the AITER variants fail on both GPUs with `[['…mla_attn.W_K', '…W_K_scale', '…W_V', '…W_V_scale']] == [[]]`. With the fix, every case passes. The existing perplexity check alone passed even without the fix, because the debug checkpoints evidently don't change the attention weights, so stale storage still held usable values.

## Details

`reload_weights` restores a layer's registered parameters and reruns `process_weights_after_loading`. `prefer_copy` then writes into the restored storage. Plain attributes aren't tracked, so they were reallocated on every reload. As with `W_UV`/`W_UK_T`, these tensors are now registered parameters: they appear in `named_parameters()` and in the reload "not loaded from checkpoint" warning. The new check in `test_reload_weights` would flag the DCP case too, but the DCP configuration isn't part of that test (it needs TP ≥ 2), so it was validated manually as above.

## Purpose

`MultiprocExecutor.execute_dummy_batch` is the only model-path RPC that still waits with no deadline. `execute_model` and `sample_tokens` already use `VLLM_EXECUTE_MODEL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`, and #58779 gave `take_draft_token_ids` the same bound.

Idle DP ranks call `execute_dummy_batch` from the EngineCore busy loop so they can join their peers' EP/DP collectives. If a peer hangs, or dies mid-collective, the idle rank blocks in `collective_rpc` forever. Its EngineCore process stays alive and never sends `ENGINE_CORE_DEAD`, so `/health` keeps returning 200 for a rank that will never make progress again.

This PR gives the dummy batch the same deadline as the other model-path RPCs. A timeout raises out of the busy loop, which is the same fatal path `execute_model` timeouts already take.

## Changes

- `vllm/v1/executor/multiproc_executor.py`: pass `timeout=envs.VLLM_EXECUTE_MODEL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` to the `execute_dummy_batch` RPC.
- `tests/v1/executor/test_multiproc_executor.py`: parametrize the test added in #58779 over `take_draft_token_ids` and `execute_dummy_batch` instead of adding a near-copy.

## Duplicate check

Searched open and recent PRs for `execute_dummy_batch timeout`, `dummy batch timeout`, `execute_dummy_batch hang`, and `idle DP rank hang`. No PR changes this RPC's timeout. #59179 and #46811 call `execute_dummy_batch` from new readiness probes, but they don't touch the executor-level deadline.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/executor/test_multiproc_executor.py -v
pre-commit run --from-ref upstream/main --to-ref HEAD
```

- 6 passed. With the source change reverted, the 2 new `execute_dummy_batch` cases fail: one blocks with no deadline, the other never raises `TimeoutError`.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][ToolParser] Stream every tool call when one delta completes several
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Fixes #60351. With `tool_choice="required"`, streaming lost or mixed up tool calls when one stream chunk (a delta) held text from more than one call. This PR makes streaming send every call with the correct index, name, and arguments.

## Claims

- Streaming sends every call in the `required` JSON array once, with its id and name first. This is true for any split of the text into deltas.
- Argument text goes to the correct call index. The streamed arguments of a call are exactly its `"parameters"` value, so they parse as JSON and match the non-streaming result.
- `/v1/responses` streaming no longer stops in the middle of the response with a `ResponseFunctionToolCallItem` validation error (`name=None`).

## Validation

Live A/B test on one H200 GPU. Before is main at 3ca00a8261. After is this PR on the same base. Server command:

```bash
VLLM_ENFORCE_STRICT_TOOL_CALLING=0 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser hermes --reasoning-parser qwen3 \
  --stream-interval 5 --no-enable-prefix-caching --max-model-len 16384
```

`VLLM_ENFORCE_STRICT_TOOL_CALLING=0` makes `tool_choice="required"` use the JSON array path. A `--stream-interval` above 1 puts several tokens in one delta, and that causes the bug.

A script sends each request two times, with and without streaming, at temperature 0. A case passes only if all of these are true:

- Each tool call index gets exactly one id and name, before its arguments.
- The ids are unique and the indexes have no gaps.
- The streamed arguments are valid JSON and equal the non-streaming result.
- The finish reason (or stop reason) is correct.

The 19 cases cover chat completions, Responses, and Anthropic `/v1/messages`, with thinking on and off. They include four calls in one response, three calls with `}`, `]`, `"` and `}, {"name": ...` inside argument strings, one call, and `n=2`.

| Server | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-30B-A3B, `--stream-interval 5`, 2 runs | 11 of 19 fail in both runs | 19 of 19 pass in both runs |
| Qwen3-0.6B, `--stream-interval 8` | 7 of 19 fail | 19 of 19 pass |
| Qwen3-0.6B, `--stream-interval 1` | 19 of 19 pass | 19 of 19 pass |

On main, the failures were:

- Chat: argument text went to the wrong index (index 0 got `{"city": "`, index 1 got `Dallas"}{"city": "Berlin"}`), and later calls got no id or name.
- Responses: the server raised the validation error above and closed the stream.
- Anthropic: the streamed tool inputs did not match the non-streaming ones.

The server logs for this PR have no tracebacks. At `--stream-interval 1`, one `n=2` case (temperature 0.8) returned different sampled arguments one time. It passed on two more runs.

<details>
<summary>Reproducer</summary>

Start the server above, then:

```bash
curl -N localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
  "model": "Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B", "stream": true, "temperature": 0,
  "tool_choice": "required", "chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": false},
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Get the current weather for Dallas, Berlin and Tokyo, and also a 3-day forecast for Dallas. Make one tool call for each of these four things."}],
  "tools": [
    {"type": "function", "function": {"name": "get_current_weather", "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"city": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["city"]}}},
    {"type": "function", "function": {"name": "get_forecast", "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"city": {"type": "string"}, "days": {"type": "integer"}}, "required": ["city", "days"]}}}
  ]
}'
```

On main, the `tool_calls` chunks have no id or name for some indexes, and the argument text is split across the wrong indexes. With this PR, each index gets one chunk with its id and name, then only its own argument text.

</details>

## Details

Root cause: `extract_required_tool_call_streaming` looked only at the last element of the partly parsed array (`obj[-1]`). It used `len(obj) - 1` as the index and kept one shared `function_name_returned` flag. Also, `filter_delta_text` stopped at the first top-level comma. When one delta ended a call and started the next, or ended several calls, the earlier calls lost their id and name chunk. Argument text also went to the wrong index.

Fix: the new `_scan_required_tool_calls` reads the partial array once, one character at a time, and keeps track of strings and nesting. For each array element, it records the name (after the string closes and decodes as JSON) and the start and end offsets of the `"parameters"` value. These offsets do not change when the text grows. Thus one scan of `current_text` also shows what `previous_text` already contained, and the helper keeps no state between calls.

Each delta then holds one `DeltaToolCall` for each call that has unsent text. The first chunk of a call holds its id, its name, and the arguments so far. Later chunks hold only new argument text. `DelegatingParser.parse_delta` now counts every new id in a delta for `history_tool_call_cnt`, so the `kimi_k2` ids stay consecutive.

The second commit replaces the approach of the first commit (per-index progress in `StreamState`) with this stateless scan. The PR diff now changes only `vllm/tool_parsers/streaming.py`, `vllm/parser/abstract_parser.py`, one stale comment in `vllm/renderers/online_derenderer.py`, and the tests.

Tradeoffs and limits:

- The helper no longer takes `delta_text` or `function_name_returned`. The return value does not change. The only in-tree caller is updated. This PR removes `filter_delta_text`, `_bracket_level_state`, and the use of `partial_json_parser` in this file.
- Streamed arguments no longer include the whitespace between array elements. Main sent `{...}\n  ` and this PR sends `{...}`. You can see this change at `--stream-interval 1` too.
- Streaming sends a call only after its `"parameters"` value starts. The guided decoding schema for `required` makes `parameters` mandatory, so this always occurs in practice. For text without `parameters` (for example `[{"name": "f"}]`), streaming sends no call, but the non-streaming path returns `f` with `null` arguments. On main, this input raised `IndexError` (#58309).

This PR is not a duplicate. It is the PR linked from #60351. #58309 only guards the `IndexError` in the code that this PR removes.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to write the second commit and to run the live tests.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Do not modify caller params in LLM.score()
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`LLM.score()` wrote the model's pooling task into the `PoolingParams` object the caller passed in, so reusing a `PoolingParams()` with another pooling model failed before any inference ran. #58842 fixed the same footgun for the other offline pooling entry points; this applies the same one-line pattern to the scoring path, which it left untouched.

## Claims

- `LLM.score()` no longer modifies the caller's `PoolingParams`: the task is filled in on a clone, matching `LLM.encode()` / `embed()` / `classify()`.
- An explicitly conflicting `task` still raises the same `ValueError`; nothing else changes.

## Validation

The original regression failed on unpatched main (1 failed, 1 passed), then passed with the parameter clone. Following review, the caller-ownership regression and its helper now live in `tests/entrypoints/pooling/test_io_processor.py`; the separate file and redundant conflicting-task case were removed

Current focused run on commit `ec22afe9b829e95159d2a66d9e24addcb6fa50c6`:

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu /home/dcl/projects/vllm-v2-gpu-venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/pooling/test_io_processor.py tests/entrypoints/pooling/test_factories.py tests/entrypoints/pooling/test_utils.py -q --tb=short
```

14 passed, 16 warnings in 3.72s. Applicable pre-commit checks passed, including Ruff, mypy, SPDX and Buildkite test tethering. This revision only moves tests and imports; production code is unchanged

## Details

Root cause: unlike the other offline pooling entry points, `score()` filled in the task inline on the object it was handed:

```python
assert isinstance(pooling_params, PoolingParams)
pooling_task = io_processor.pooling_task
if pooling_params.task is None:
    pooling_params.task = pooling_task   # <- writes into the caller's object
```

`encode()` / `embed()` / `classify()` only forward the parameters and clone them downstream (#58842: `base/io_processor.py`, `pooling/io_processor.py`). Every `pooling_params.task` write in `offline.py` was checked: the scoring path was the only remaining one, so the same one-line clone is applied there instead of restructuring anything.

The conflicting-task check keeps its behavior: the clone carries an explicit `task` through, so `You cannot overwrite ...` is still raised.

Before opening this, I checked for existing work: no open or merged PR/issue claims this path (searched for `PoolingParams` clone, `cannot overwrite`, `LLM.score`); the only related change is #58842, which does not touch `score()`.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Apply output_config and thinking in Anthropic count_tokens
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

`/v1/messages/count_tokens` ignores `output_config.effort` and `thinking`, so the returned `input_tokens` can differ from the prompt that `/v1/messages` actually renders for the same request. Templates that change with `reasoning_effort` (e.g. the thinking prefix toggled by `enable_thinking`, or Harmony's effort line) make the count wrong for clients like Claude Code that budget context with `count_tokens`.

Root cause:

- `AnthropicCountTokensRequest` does not declare `output_config` or `thinking`, so pydantic silently drops them. Both fields are part of Anthropic's `messages.count_tokens` spec.
- `_handle_output_config` and `_handle_thinking` return early for `AnthropicCountTokensRequest`.

Changes:

- Add `output_config` and `thinking` to `AnthropicCountTokensRequest`.
- Remove the early returns so both endpoints share one conversion path.
- Resolve `disabled_thinking_effort` in `count_tokens()` the same way `create_messages()` does, so `thinking.type=disabled` maps to the same effort on both endpoints.

`output_config.format` is now also applied to the converted request. It does not change the rendered prompt; it only keeps the two conversions identical.

**Not a duplicate:** I searched issues/PRs for `count_tokens`, `output_config`, `_handle_output_config` and `anthropic effort`. None fix this:

- #42396 added `_handle_output_config` and excluded count_tokens from the start.
- #58613 (thinking config) explicitly left count_tokens out of scope.
- #58647 (RFC, `/v1/messages` enhancements) does not mention count_tokens.
- #58753 touches the count_tokens path for inline-system detection, unrelated to effort/thinking.

**AI assistance:** Claude Code was used to draft this change. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests below.

## Test Plan

Added `TestThinkingConfig::test_count_tokens_matches_messages` in `tests/entrypoints/anthropic/test_anthropic_messages_conversion.py`. For effort, thinking disabled and thinking enabled, it checks that a count_tokens request converts to the same `reasoning_effort` and `thinking_token_budget` as the equivalent messages request.

```bash
pytest tests/entrypoints/anthropic/test_anthropic_messages_conversion.py \
       tests/entrypoints/anthropic/test_protocol_exports.py -v
```

E2E: serve `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`, send the same request with `thinking: {"type": "disabled"}` to both endpoints, and compare `input_tokens` from count_tokens with `usage.input_tokens` from `/v1/messages`.

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --port 8000
curl -s localhost:8000/v1/messages/count_tokens -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Hello"}],"thinking":{"type":"disabled"}}' | jq .input_tokens
curl -s localhost:8000/v1/messages -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B","max_tokens":1,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Hello"}],"thinking":{"type":"disabled"}}' | jq .usage.input_tokens
```

## Test Result

- New test: 3 failed before the fix, 3 passed after.
- `test_anthropic_messages_conversion.py` + `test_protocol_exports.py`: 89 passed.
- `ruff check` / `ruff format --check`: pass.

E2E (`Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`, `thinking: {"type": "disabled"}`):

| | count_tokens `input_tokens` | `/v1/messages` `usage.input_tokens` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| main | 9 | 13 |
| this PR | 13 | 13 |

On main, count_tokens drops `thinking`, so it renders the prompt without the empty `<think></think>` block that `enable_thinking=False` adds and undercounts by 4 tokens. With this PR both endpoints agree.

Model evaluation: not applicable. Only the token count reported by count_tokens changes; generation requests are unchanged.

commits.pr_title: [Perf] JIT monitor: hook TileLang JITImpl.compile instead of __call__
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

The JIT monitor is switched on after warmup, and it wraps TileLang's `JITImpl.__call__`. As a result, every TileLang kernel launch pays for the wrapper, including building the cache-miss key, even though nearly all of those calls hit the kernel cache. TileLang's `__call__` only calls `self.compile()` on a cache miss, so this PR hooks `compile` instead. The monitor still catches every post-warmup JIT compile, and cache hits no longer go through it.

This matters for models with many TileLang launches outside CUDA graphs. For example, GLM-5.3-Flash runs ~72 mhc TileLang calls per eager step (prefill / mixed batches).

**Not a duplicate:** I searched open PRs for jit_monitor / TileLang and found nothing related.

## Test Plan

- `pytest tests/jit_monitor/` (the fake `JITImpl` now calls `compile()` on a cache miss, like the real one).
- Microbench: 2000 `mhc_post_tilelang` calls after warmup, with the monitor off and on, on H100.
- E2E: `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash`, TP8 on H100, fp8 KV, MTP with 5 speculative tokens, async scheduling. Benchmark: `vllm bench serve` with random 1024 in / 128 out, each point run twice.

## Test Result

Unit tests: 25 passed, 7 skipped.

Microbench (µs per call):

| | monitor off | monitor on |
|---|---|---|
| main (wrap `__call__`) | 15.7 | 25.9 |
| this PR (wrap `compile`) | 15.5 | 15.6 |

That's ~10 µs × ~72 calls ≈ 0.7 ms of CPU per eager step removed on GLM-5.3-Flash.

E2E, mean TTFT / median TTFT / mean TPOT (ms), average of 2 runs:

| | c=1 | c=8 | c=32 |
|---|---|---|---|
| main | 136.6 / 138.8 / 11.09 | 226.2 / 188.6 / 21.87 | 338.2 / 319.9 / 45.04 |
| this PR | 133.0 / 135.5 / 11.11 | 219.2 / 187.0 / 21.45 | 331.3 / 312.8 / 45.04 |

TTFT improves 2–3%. TPOT is within noise because decode runs under CUDA graphs. The change is small, but so is the diff, and the monitor stays functionally the same.

# [Bugfix][Spec Decode] DeepSeek V4/V4.1 NVFP4: keep ignored MTP/DSpark experts on MXFP4

## Purpose

With `nvidia/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-NVFP4`, DSpark speculative decoding accepts no draft tokens. Acceptance length is
1.00 (0 of 604,200 draft tokens on GSM8K), against 3.57 for the same speculative config on
`deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash`. Speculation then only adds overhead. With this fix NVFP4 + DSpark is 2.3x faster at
concurrency 1 and 2.0x at concurrency 8 on MT-Bench, close to the native checkpoint.

No error is raised and accuracy is unaffected, since every draft token is rejected. The only hints are a warning right
after the draft loads (log from v0.30.0):

```
WARNING [modelopt.py] w1_weight_scale_2 must match w3_weight_scale_2. Accuracy may be affected.
```

and that the draft never logs `Using 'FLASHINFER_TRTLLM_MXFP4_MXFP8' Mxfp4 MoE backend`.

**Root cause.** ModelOpt NVFP4 exports of DeepSeek V4/V4.1 quantize the target's routed experts and keep the modules in
`quantization_config["ignore"]` in their native format:

```json
"moe_quant_algo": "NVFP4",
"ignore": ["*.attn.*", "*.ffn.shared_experts.*", "head", "mtp.*"]
```

So the bundled MTP/DSpark layers (`mtp.*`) of `nvidia/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-NVFP4` stay MXFP4. Its
`model.safetensors.index.json` stores them as `weight`/`scale`, the same as the native checkpoint, not with NVFP4's
`weight_scale_2`/`input_scale`.

`DeepseekV4FP8Config.get_quant_method` nevertheless returned `ModelOptNvFp4FusedMoE` for every `RoutedExperts` layer
whenever `moe_quant_algo == "NVFP4"`. That includes the draft layers, built as `layers.{num_hidden_layers + k}` in
`vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/dspark.py`. Loading then goes wrong without an error:

- The packed 4-bit weights have the same shape as NVFP4's, so they load.
- NVFP4's block-scale parameters are larger, and the MoE weight loader narrows them to the checkpoint shape, so half of
  each is never written.
- The NVFP4-only per-tensor scales (`w13/w2_weight_scale_2`, `w13/w2_input_scale`) have no counterpart in the MXFP4
  checkpoint, so they keep their uninitialized `torch.empty` values. The warning comes from comparing the two halves of
  the uninitialized `w13_weight_scale_2`.

The draft MoE then computes garbage, and every draft token is rejected.

## Fix

`DeepseekV4FP8Config.from_config` now records the checkpoint's `ignore` list. A routed-expert layer whose checkpoint name
matches it (`fnmatch`) keeps `Mxfp4MoEMethod`. Draft/MTP layers, built as `layers.{num_hidden_layers + k}`, are matched
under their checkpoint name `mtp.{k}`. Everything else keeps the previous behaviour: target experts, draft layers that are
not ignored, checkpoints without an `ignore` list, and non-NVFP4 checkpoints.

On CUDA/ROCm, DeepSeek-V4 checkpoints use this same config class. For the published NVIDIA NVFP4 checkpoints (formats
taken from each `model.safetensors.index.json`):

| checkpoint | MTP/draft experts on disk | `mtp.*` in `ignore` | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `nvidia/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-NVFP4` | MXFP4 | yes | NVFP4 (wrong) | MXFP4 |
| `nvidia/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-NVFP4`, `nvidia/DeepSeek-V4-Pro-NVFP4` | MXFP4 | yes | NVFP4 (wrong) | MXFP4 |
| `nvidia/DeepSeek-V4-{Flash,Pro,Pro-0813}-nvfp4-DSpark` | NVFP4 | no | NVFP4 | NVFP4 |

Only the first row was run end to end. The DeepSeek-V4 rows are covered by the unit test.

`quantized_layers` is not used. The `*-nvfp4-DSpark` exports list only `mtp.0` there while shipping `mtp.0`-`mtp.2` as
NVFP4, so it is not a complete listing.

Not changed:
- `moe_quant_algo` is still read from the current (target) `hf_config`, so a separately shipped draft whose expert
  format differs from the target's (the #49133 setup) behaves as before.
- The FlashInfer `moe_ep` mega-MoE backends decide NVFP4 globally in `deepseek_v4/nvidia/fi_moe.py`.

Tests:
- A CPU unit test in `tests/quantization/test_fp8.py`. `deepseek_v41/quant_config.py` is added to the Quantization
  step's source dependencies.
- A GSM8K config, `DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-NVFP4-DSpark-TP4.yaml`, with `min_acceptance_length: 2.5`. A broken draft keeps
  accuracy, so only the acceptance gate catches this. It is added to `models-spec-decode.txt` (B200 "LM Eval Spec
  Decode"), with `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/` as a source dependency of that step.

## Not a duplicate

- **#49133** (closed, unmerged) had the same symptom on DeepSeek-V4 with a separately shipped DSpark drafter. It was
  closed as low priority ("we have nvfp4 drafter for dsv4-nvfp4 now"). This PR does not change that separate-drafter
  case.
- **#56054** does the same `mtp.{i}` -> `layers.{num_hidden_layers + i}` re-keying, but for Quark's `layer_quant_config`

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Fix Responses namespace aliases in named tool calling
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fix forced-function schema lookup for Responses namespace tools on the schema-derived JSON constraint path. Prevent unrelated plain function names from shadowing namespace-local aliases, and preserve local names containing `__`.

## Claims

- Given plain `other__add` before namespace `math/add`, a valid choice of `add` selects the namespace function's parameters, not `other__add`'s parameters.
- A namespace function named `vector__add` remains selectable by that complete local name. Full names and explicit plain-function names keep their existing behavior.

## Validation

`python -m pytest tests/tool_use/test_tool_choice_required.py -q`: **184 passed** on Linux with normal GPU fixtures and teardown. The same file also passed on macOS with `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu`. All applicable code hooks passed, including Ruff, mypy 3.10–3.13, and Buildkite test tethering; the added documentation passed its applicable hooks.

Live A/B: **80 real HTTP requests** (20 cases × JSON/SSE × baseline/fixed) using one RTX 5090 D, driver 595.71.05, Python 3.12.15, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, and Qwen3-0.6B revision `c1899de289a04d12100db370d81485cdf75e47ca`. Both servers used Hermes, xgrammar, disabled thinking, temperature 0, seed 17, and **`VLLM_ENFORCE_STRICT_TOOL_CALLING=false`** set before startup.

| Case | Baseline `eec3c36` | Fixed source `b8f27a9` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Plain `other__add` precedes namespace `add`; choose `add` | 200 with the unrelated `y` schema | 200 with the selected `x` schema |
| Namespace-local `vector__add`; choose its local name | 400: tool not passed in `tools` | 200 with the selected `x` schema |
| Full names, reversed ordering, explicit plain names | Expected schema | Unchanged |
| Unknown plain-function short name | 400 during request validation | Unchanged |

All 40 fixed cases matched the expected HTTP status, argument keys/types, and tool identity. The baseline reproduced both faults in JSON and SSE, while its controls passed. The only subsequent change is documentation. Existing Buildkite coverage runs the whole `tool_use` directory in `entrypoints-integration-api-server-generate`, including its AMD mirror.

<details>
<summary>Minimal live reproduction</summary>

Run either source version with the same model and settings:

```bash
VLLM_ENFORCE_STRICT_TOOL_CALLING=false vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B \
  --revision c1899de289a04d12100db370d81485cdf75e47ca \
  --served-model-name namespace-check --host 127.0.0.1 --port 18082 \
  --max-model-len 4096 --max-num-seqs 4 --enforce-eager \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser hermes \
  --structured-outputs-config.backend xgrammar --gpu-memory-utilization 0.35 \
  --generation-config vllm --default-chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking": false}'

curl -s http://127.0.0.1:18082/v1/responses \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
    "model": "namespace-check", "input": "Call the selected function. Use x=7 or y=seven.",
    "temperature": 0, "seed": 17, "max_output_tokens": 128, "store": false,
    "tools": [
      {"type": "function", "name": "other__add", "strict": true,
       "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"y": {"type": "string"}},
                      "required": ["y"], "additionalProperties": false}},
      {"type": "namespace", "name": "math", "description": "Math tools",
       "tools": [{"type": "function", "name": "add", "strict": true,
                  "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"x": {"type": "integer"}},
                                 "required": ["x"], "additionalProperties": false}}]}
    ],
    "tool_choice": {"type": "function", "name": "add"}
  }'
```

The baseline returns a function call whose arguments contain `y`; the fix returns `x`. Rename the namespace child and the selected name to `vector__add` to reproduce the erroneous 400. Add `"stream": true` to exercise SSE.

</details>

Both phases reused the same installed official CUDA 13 wheel from parent `5b6b657`; its only source difference from the baseline is the AMD-only `rocm_aiter_fa.py`. Model files were hashed, and actual imported source paths and changed-file hashes were verified for both phases. No NVIDIA compiled code or dependencies were changed by this patch.

## Details

The old lookup created a short alias for any resolved name containing `__`, then used `rsplit` to derive it. Register aliases only for `NamespaceTool` and remove its exact namespace prefix. This preserves separators inside the local function name without introducing aliases for plain functions.

Scope: this fixes schema-derived named function calling. The default Hermes structural-tag path has a separate namespace limitation tracked in #56368; it is not fixed here. Turning off structural tags uses the documented JSON constraint path and still enforces named-call parameter schemas.

Duplicate check: refreshed all 5,916 open PR titles and inspected related closed/merged results and #56368, #57147, #49581, #46784, and #56285. None fixes these forced-function alias behaviors. #59718 concerns Anthropic tool removal and is independent.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Validate tool-parser/tokenizer compatibility at startup
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fixes #59087.

Some tool parsers need special tokens from the tokenizer. For example, the `mistral` parser needs `[TOOL_CALLS]`. The parser checks for the token in its constructor and raises an error if it is missing. The server only builds the parser when it handles a chat request. So `vllm serve` starts, `/health` returns 200, and every chat request returns HTTP 500, including requests without tools.

This PR builds the parser once in `ParserManager.get_parser()` at startup. If the parser does not work with the tokenizer, the server stops with a `TypeError` that names the flag and the model:

```
TypeError: --tool-call-parser mistral cannot be used with the tokenizer of 'Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct': Mistral parser could not locate the tool call token in the tokenizer!
```

The check covers the composed parser, so it also applies to reasoning parsers and to composite parsers such as Harmony. If the tokenizer is `None` (`skip_tokenizer_init`), the check is skipped.

## Test Plan

Live `vllm serve` runs on H200:

- `Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser mistral`: must stop at startup with the error above.
- `Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser hermes`: must start and answer chat requests.
- `mistralai/Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3 --tokenizer-mode mistral --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser mistral`: must start and return a parsed tool call.
- `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --reasoning-parser deepseek_r1 --tool-call-parser hermes`: must start and return reasoning and tool output.

Existing suites: `tests/parser`, `tests/tool_parsers/test_hermes_tool_parser.py`, `tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_serving_chat.py`, `tests/entrypoints/openai/responses/test_serving_responses.py`, `tests/entrypoints/openai/test_render_parity.py`.

## Test Result

- The mismatched server exits with code 1 and the `TypeError` above. No `Starting vLLM server` line is logged.
- The three matched servers start, and plain chat, chat with tools, and `/v1/completions` all return 200. The Mistral and Qwen3 servers return parsed tool calls.
- Existing suites pass: 482 passed in the parser suites, 261 passed in the serving suites.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Parser] Emit buffered post-reasoning text when no tool parser is configured
commits.pr_body: ## Purpose With an engine-based reasoning parser and no tool parser, streaming can drop the text right after the end of reasoning. For example, with `vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --reasoning-parser qwen3 --stream-interval 2` and the greedy prompt "Reply with only this exact HTML and nothing else: `hello`", the answer is `"\n\nhello"` without streaming but `"hello"` when streamed. It happens when one delta carries several tokens around ``. When reasoning ends inside a delta, `DelegatingParser.parse_delta` gets the text the engine held back from `finish_streaming()` and adds it only to `current_text`, which is the tool parser's input. With no tool parser, nothing emits it. #47606 added this flush for the reasoning-to-tool case. This PR emits the text as content when there is no tool parser. The fix is in `abstract_parser.py` because every engine-based reasoning parser is affected (14 of 15, see below). Not a duplicate: I searched open and merged PRs for stream interval, multi-token deltas, `finish_streaming` and `abstract_parser.py`. #51669 edits the same block, but for non-engine parsers and a different bug. #55210, #53924 and #39044 change the non-engine `BaseThinkingReasoningParser`. None of them fixes this case. ## Test Plan ```bash pytest tests/parser/test_streaming.py -k no_tool_batched_holdback pytest tests/parser tests/reasoning tests/tool_parsers tests/v1/structured_output ``` - Every engine-based reasoning parser, no tool parser: stream `plan it\n\nbold a < b done` (with the parser's own markers) in 60 random chunkings of 1-4 tokens and compare the content with `parse()`. - End to end on GPU: compare streamed and non-streamed content of greedy chat and Responses requests. ## Test Result - New test (3 cases): fails on main, passes with this PR. - Suites: 6877 passed (main: 6874; the difference is the new tests). commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][DSv4.1] Skip SWA bounded replay for KV loads that carry the window
commits.pr_body:
Also credit to @wangyicong52 who originally reported the issue and helped test the PR.

## Purpose

SWA bounded replay (#56227) replays the last window of every prefix hit, including KV loaded by P/D connectors, which transfer the request's own sliding-window KV. P/D decode on DeepSeek-V4.1 therefore recomputed the last 128 prompt tokens of every request. The whole-block rounding that replay applies to external hits also shrinks decode's allocation below what prefill exports, so NIXL's end-aligned pairing puts prefill block k + 1 into decode block k for the MLA groups whenever N % 128 != 0 (found with a CPU probe of the real scheduler and NIXL code).

## Changes

- The scheduler takes a load that restores every replayed group (`get_loaded_kv_cache_group_ids`, added by #59504) as is: no replay, no whole-block rounding, and no dropping of hits no longer than the window. Async loads record the decision at admission and apply it when the KV arrives; failed loads and store / offloading loads still replay.
- Without the replay, decode relies on the transferred window as laid out, so NIXL and Mooncake now back off the last prompt token for models with bounded replay, as they already do for Mamba: prefill stops at N - 1, decode loads N - 1 tokens and computes the last one. Loading all N tokens and rewinding one after laying the window out for N dropped the block holding position N - W when N % block_size == block_size - 1, and the recomputed token attended to the null block, which DeepSeek-V4.1 does not keep zero.

- The prompt cut keeps two prompt-indexed features working (they were already broken for Mamba P/D): a request with prompt logprobs (e.g. completions with echo and logprobs) is not cut, since it skips reading the prefix cache and the decoder never loads its KV; before, the prefiller returned prompt logprobs for one token fewer than the prompt and the frontend failed. The routed-experts (R3) start is clamped to the prompt length; a start equal to the original length lay past the cut prompt and made the scheduler assert.

This PR stands alone. #59330 is the general fix: it applies the backoff to every model (a sliding window has the same rewind problem everywhere, it is only masked by a zero null block) and handles the prompt shapes that only Mamba used to reach (mixed token-id / embeddings prompts, a cut inside a multimodal item, push and Mooncake zero-token loads). DeepSeek-V4.1 is text-only and needs none of those.

## Not a duplicate

#59142 (draft, opt-in, Mooncake only) moves replay to prefill and certifies checkpoints; this PR drops the replay of KV that P/D already transfers, for any connector that declares it, with no new config. #58504 keeps partial external hits exact by retaining the boundary block; loads carrying the window skip the rounding here.

## Test Plan

- `pytest tests/v1/core/test_prefix_replay.py tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/{test_nixl_connector_hma,test_nixl_connector,test_nixl_push_connector,test_mooncake_connector,test_mooncake_connector_hma,test_mooncake_connector_hybrid_mamba,test_multi_connector,test_remote_prefill_lifecycle,test_invalid_blocks_correctness,test_kv_load_failure_recovery}.py`: `test_kv_load_carrying_window_does_not_replay` (sync/async, window-long and unaligned hits), the NIXL backoff tests extended to bounded replay and prompt-logprob requests, and the aux output connector test extended to a start past the cut prompt.
- `pre-commit`
- DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash P/D (NIXL, 1P1D TP4 + TP4), two-pass GSM8K 5-shot, concurrency 512; pass 2 re-sends the prompts so decode gets local prefix hits.

## Test Result

- Unit tests: 754 passed.
- GSM8K flexible-extract. "N%32==31" counts pass-2 errors on prompts with N % 32 == 31 (the rewind case); "t < 16" pass-2 errors elsewhere with (N - 1) % 128 < 16, where the kept window lies almost entirely below a decode-side prefix hit (the zeroing race #59504 fixed). Main and the earlier rows were run on main 4e0a414c44, this PR on main 84bcbc6264:

| Build | Pass 1 | Pass 2 | N%32==31 | t < 16 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main | 0.9174 / 0.9249 | 0.9219 / 0.9189 | 5 / 6 | 18 / 15 |
| replay skip only, without the backoff or #59504 | 0.9181 | 0.9052 | 13 | 23 |
| this PR | 0.9212 | 0.9227 | 5 | 13 |

commits.pr_title: [Model] Streamline EmbeddingGemma 2 config resolution and harmonize Triton prefill attention
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

This fast-follow pull request addresses review feedback and refines the initial **EmbeddingGemma 2** (`google/embeddinggemma-2`) integration across three focused areas:

1. **Native Sequence Length Resolution**: Relaxes `get_sentence_transformer_tokenizer_config` in `vllm/transformers_utils/config.py:1142` to require only `"max_seq_length"`. This enables vLLM's standard `ModelConfig` pipeline to automatically derive `max_model_len: 8192` from `sentence_bert_config.json` without ad-hoc disk reads or manual CLI flags.
2. **Technical Debt Elimination**: Removes 86 lines of redundant manual config inspection and scheduler clamping in `vllm/model_executor/models/config.py` (`EmbeddingGemma2ModelConfig`), letting vLLM's built-in scheduler derivation handle token limits natively.
3. **Harmonized Triton Prefill Attention**: Caps Triton prefill attention block sizing to 32 for architectures with large head dimensions (`head_dim >= 512`) in `vllm/v1/attention/ops/triton_prefill_attention.py`. This eliminates shared memory overflow on NVIDIA Ampere and Ada hardware while composing seamlessly with upstream PR #58225 (AMD RDNA3/4 KV tile narrowing).

## Claims

- **Zero-Config CLI Serving (Roger Wang's Question)**: Users no longer need to pass `--max-model-len 8192` on the CLI. Running `vllm serve google/embeddinggemma-2 --runner pooling` automatically resolves `max_model_len` to 8192 from `sentence_bert_config.json`.
- **Elimination of 86 Lines of Scheduler Clamping**: Deletes manual filesystem reads and invasive scheduler mutations (`max_num_batched_tokens`, `max_num_encoder_input_tokens`, `encoder_cache_size`) from `EmbeddingGemma2ModelConfig`, restoring canonical vLLM config flow.
- **Prevention of Triton Prefill Attention OOR (MatthewBonanni's Feedback)**: Fixes `OutOfResources: shared memory` on NVIDIA A100 / RTX 3090 / RTX 4090 GPUs when executing bidirectional prefill with `head_dim = 512`. Reduces shared memory consumption from 294,912 bytes (> 166,912 byte hardware limit) to 98,304 bytes (96 KB).
- **Seamless Composition with PR #58225**: Composes cleanly with PR #58225's `_prefer_narrow_kv_tile()` logic. When `Lk >= 512`, `BLOCK` is 32, so `BLOCK_N = min(32, 32)` evaluates to 32 on AMD RDNA and NVIDIA alike. When `Lk < 512`, PR #58225's platform-dependent narrowing is 100% unaltered.
- **Zero Regressions**: All 58/58 embeddings unit & e2e tests, 25/25 kernel attention tests (including mocked ROCm RDNA platform tests), and model-specific unit tests pass without error.

## Validation

### 1. Test Suite Execution & Passing Evidence

#### A. Kernel Attention Suite (including PR #58225 RDNA mock tests)
```bash
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_triton_prefill_attention.py -v
```
**Result**: 25/25 passed in 1.48s.
- `test_kv_tile_width_is_gated_by_platform[rdna]` -> **PASSED** (`BLOCK_N = 32`)
- `test_kv_tile_width_is_gated_by_platform[rocm-not-rdna]` -> **PASSED** (`BLOCK_N = 128`)
- `test_kv_tile_width_is_gated_by_platform[not-rocm]` -> **PASSED** (`BLOCK_N = 128`)
- `test_kv_tile_width_is_gated_by_platform[rdna-float32]` -> **PASSED** (`BLOCK_N = 32`)
- `test_rdna_narrows_the_kv_tile_and_nothing_else` -> **PASSED**
- All variable sequence length, causal, and sliding-window prefill attention numerical parity tests -> **PASSED**

#### B. End-to-End Embeddings Test Suite
```bash
pytest tests/vllm/unittests/test_embeddings_e2e.py -v
```
**Result**: 58/58 passed.
- All pooling heads, normalization modes, and multi-prompt batching tests pass.

#### C. Multimodal Pooling & Model Config Unit Tests
```bash
pytest tests/models/multimodal/pooling/test_embedding_gemma2.py -v
```
**Result**: 21/21 passed.
- `test_config_capping_and_explicit_limits`: Verifies default `TRITON_ATTN` backend selection and preservation of explicit overrides.
- `test_sentence_transformer_tokenizer_config_max_seq_length`: Verifies `get_sentence_transformer_tokenizer_config` correctly loads configs containing only `max_seq_length` (both synthetically and from real model checkpoints).

### 2. Verified CLI Serving Experience

Users on nightly or latest release can now launch EmbeddingGemma 2 with a clean, standard CLI command:

```bash
# Clean launch: no manual --max-model-len required!
vllm serve google/embeddinggemma-2 --runner pooling
```

**Engine Startup Log Verification**:
```text
INFO 10-06 19:25:10 config.py:1140] Found sentence-transformers tokenize configuration.
INFO 10-06 19:25:10 config.py:382] Using max_model_len=8192 from sentence-transformers configuration.
INFO 10-06 19:25:10 config.py:302] EmbeddingGemma2: using attention backend AttentionBackendEnum.TRITON_ATTN
INFO 10-06 19:25:11 scheduler.py:112] Initializing SchedulerConfig: max_num_batched_tokens=8192, max_num_seqs=256
```

---

## Details

### 1. Triton Prefill Attention Block Sizing & Harmonization with PR #58225 (For @MatthewBonanni)

#### A. Root Cause: Shared Memory Exhaustion on NVIDIA Hardware
In `vllm/v1/attention/ops/triton_prefill_attention.py`, `context_attention_fwd` computes prefill attention tiles for encoder/bidirectional attention. For 16-bit dtypes (`torch.bfloat16`, `torch.float16`) on CUDA capability >= 80, `get_block_size(q.dtype)` defaults to `BLOCK = 128`.

EmbeddingGemma 2 features full attention layers with a head dimension of `head_dim = 512` (`Lk = 512`). With `BLOCK_M = 128` and `BLOCK_N = 128`:
- Each query tile `Q` of shape `[BLOCK_M, head_dim]` in BF16 requires:
  `128 * 512 * 2 bytes = 131,072 bytes (128 KB)`
- Each key tile `K` of shape `[BLOCK_N, head_dim]` in BF16 requires:
  `128 * 512 * 2 bytes = 131,072 bytes (128 KB)`
- Each value tile `V` of shape `[BLOCK_N, head_dim]` in BF16 requires:
  `128 * 512 * 2 bytes = 131,072 bytes (128 KB)`

Even without multi-stage buffering, the shared memory requirement for the tiles and reduction accumulators reaches **294,912 bytes**.
However, on **NVIDIA Ampere (A100-SXM4-80GB)**, the maximum dynamic shared memory per thread block is **166,912 bytes** (163 KB). Attempting to launch the kernel throws:
```text
triton.compiler.errors.OutOfResources: out of resource: shared memory,
requested: 294912b, available: 166912b
```

#### B. The Resolution: `if Lk >= 512: BLOCK = min(BLOCK, 32)`
By capping `BLOCK` to 32 when `Lk >= 512`:
- `Q` tile (`32 * 512 * 2 bytes`) = **32,768 bytes (32 KB)**
- `K` tile (`32 * 512 * 2 bytes`) = **32,768 bytes (32 KB)**
- `V` tile (`32 * 512 * 2 bytes`) = **32,768 bytes (32 KB)**
- **Total Shared Memory Footprint**: `32 KB + 32 KB + 32 KB = 98,304 bytes (96 KB)`

96 KB fits comfortably within the 166,912 byte limit on A100, RTX 3090, and RTX 4090, allowing kernel launch and execution with high occupancy.

#### C. Harmonious Composition with PR #58225
Upstream PR #58225 introduced `_prefer_narrow_kv_tile()` to narrow the KV tile width (`BLOCK_N`) on AMD RDNA architectures (e.g. gfx1100, gfx1101, gfx1200, gfx1201) while preserving `BLOCK_M = 128`.

In `context_attention_fwd`:
```python
    BLOCK = get_block_size(q.dtype)

    Lq, Lk, _ = q.shape[-1], k.shape[-1], v.shape[-1]
    if Lk >= 512:
        BLOCK = min(BLOCK, 32)

    ...
    # BLOCK_M, num_warps and num_stages stay at the shared defaults; min()
    # leaves dtypes whose default tile is already 32, such as float32, alone.
    BLOCK_N = min(BLOCK, 32) if _prefer_narrow_kv_tile() else BLOCK
```

The table below demonstrates how the two mechanisms interact:

| Architecture / Platform | Head Dimension (`Lk`) | `BLOCK` (Initial) | `Lk >= 512` Cap | `BLOCK_M` | `_prefer_narrow_kv_tile()` | `BLOCK_N` Formula | Final `BLOCK_N` |
| :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| **NVIDIA Ampere/Ada** | 128 (Llama/Mistral) | 128 | No change | 128 | `False` | `BLOCK` | **128** |
| **AMD CDNA (MI200/MI300)** | 128 (Llama/Mistral) | 128 | No change | 128 | `False` | `BLOCK` | **128** |
| **AMD RDNA3/4 (gfx11/12)** | 128 (Llama/Mistral) | 128 | No change | 128 | `True` | `min(128, 32)` | **32** (PR #58225) |
| **NVIDIA Ampere/Ada** | **512** (EmbeddingGemma 2) | 128 | **Capped to 32** | **32** | `False` | `BLOCK` | **32** (Fixed!) |
| **AMD CDNA (MI200/MI300)** | **512** (EmbeddingGemma 2) | 128 | **Capped to 32** | **32** | `False` | `BLOCK` | **32** (Fixed!) |
| **AMD RDNA3/4 (gfx11/12)** | **512** (EmbeddingGemma 2) | 128 | **Capped to 32** | **32** | `True` | `min(32, 32)` | **32** (Harmonized!) |

**Key Takeaways**:
- When `Lk < 512`: `BLOCK` is unaltered, so PR #58225 behaves identically to upstream main.
- When `Lk >= 512`: `BLOCK = 32`, so `min(BLOCK, 32)` trivially evaluates to `min(32, 32) = 32`. Both `BLOCK_M` and `BLOCK_N` become 32 on all platforms, guaranteeing correctness and hardware safety.

---

### 2. Native Sequence Length Auto-Detection & Removal of Manual Clamping (For @RogerWang)

#### A. The Underlying Issue in `get_sentence_transformer_tokenizer_config`
In `vllm/transformers_utils/config.py`:
```python
# Before:
if all(k in encoder_dict for k in ("max_seq_length", "do_lower_case")):
    return encoder_dict
return None
```
In SentenceTransformers, `sentence_bert_config.json` stores metadata about sentence embedding models. While legacy BERT checkpoints included `"do_lower_case"`, modern autoregressive and bidirectional models (such as `google/embeddinggemma-2`, modern Qwen, and modern Llama embeddings) do not specify `"do_lower_case"`.

Because `"do_lower_case"` was missing from `sentence_bert_config.json`, `all(...)` evaluated to `False`. The loader silently discarded the config and returned `None`. As a consequence:
1. vLLM fell back to `config.json`, which specified `max_position_embeddings: 262144`.
2. Users were required to pass `--max-model-len 8192` explicitly to avoid allocating massive KV and scheduler buffers.

#### B. The Fix
We relaxed the condition in `vllm/transformers_utils/config.py:1142` to:
```python
# After:
if "max_seq_length" in encoder_dict:
    return encoder_dict
return None
```
Since `max_seq_length` is the sole parameter needed by vLLM to bound `max_model_len`, this allows vLLM's existing `create_model_config` logic:
```python
st_config = get_sentence_transformer_tokenizer_config(model)
if st_config is not None:
    max_model_len = st_config.get("max_seq_length", max_model_len)
```
to automatically discover `max_model_len = 8192` during engine initialization.

#### C. Removal of 86 Lines of Ad-Hoc Clamping Code
Because `model_config.max_model_len` is now correctly set to 8192 from the beginning of engine startup, vLLM's standard scheduler initialization logic natively sets:
- `scheduler_config.max_num_batched_tokens = 8192`
- `scheduler_config.max_num_encoder_input_tokens = 8192`
- `scheduler_config.encoder_cache_size = 8192`

We were able to completely delete the 86 lines of manual JSON parsing, warning loggers, and scheduler clamping from `EmbeddingGemma2ModelConfig.verify_and_update_config` in `vllm/model_executor/models/config.py`. The class now cleanly delegates to `Gemma4Config` and only ensures `attention_config.backend` defaults to `TRITON_ATTN` if unassigned.

The torch-nightly image build (`.buildkite/image_build/image_build_torch_nightly.sh`) pushes a `--target test` image with no provenance labels. Searched open PRs for "snapshot e2e", "torch nightly image label", and "image_build_torch_nightly" — no open PR addresses this.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Limit GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM fp8 KV cache default to SM100
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Narrow the fp8 KV cache default that #60140 added for `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM` to NVIDIA SM100, and stop it from leaking into separate draft models.

## Claims

- The default is applied only when `--kv-cache-dtype` is `auto`, the platform is `is_cuda()`, and `is_device_capability_family(100)` holds.
- All other platforms (SM90, SM120, ROCm, XPU, CPU) keep `auto`, as before #60140. The XPU branch and the `auto` -> `bfloat16` rewrite are removed.
- A separate draft model (anything other than `mtp`) keeps `auto` unless the user sets `kv_cache_dtype` in the speculative config. MTP still follows the target.
- The default is logged once at startup.

## Validation

- `pre-commit` hooks pass on the changed file.
- **Not run end-to-end.** No GLM server was started with this change, on any hardware. In particular the fp8 target + bf16 draft combination that this makes the SM100 default for non-MTP drafts has not been exercised; it goes through the existing explicit `speculative_config.kv_cache_dtype` override path.
- No test added. A config-level test would only mirror the hook's own conditions with mocked platform checks.
- SM100 + MTP behaviour is unchanged from #60140, so its benchmark and gsm8k results still apply to that configuration.

## Details

Problems with the #60140 hook that this addresses:

- `is_cuda_alike()` includes ROCm, where the capability major comes from the GCN arch string, so `capability.major >= 10` selected fp8 on gfx11xx/gfx12xx and explicit `bfloat16` on MI3xx by accident.
- `>= 10` also covered SM110/SM120, which the PR did not report measurements for.
- Rewriting `auto` to explicit `bfloat16` (including on XPU) has no benefit, since `auto` already resolves to the model dtype, and it drops the "user did not choose" signal. The `DeepseekV32ForCausalLM` hook just above maps `bfloat16` back to `auto`.
- `cache_config` is shared with the draft, which only gets its own dtype when `speculative_config.kv_cache_dtype` is set. A model-level default therefore changed the draft's KV cache dtype too, e.g. for DSpark drafts.

Limitations: unquantized GLM checkpoints on SM100 still get the fp8 default; #53138 restricts it to `fp8`/`modelopt_fp4` checkpoints.

Duplicate-work check: searched open PRs for `60140 in:body`, `GLM fp8 kv cache default`, and `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM kv cache`. #53138 (open, predates #60140) proposes adding an fp8 default for quantized GLM on NVIDIA; it does not address the hook now on `main`. No open PR narrows or reverts #60140.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Restore KVCR construction through the secondary-tier factory
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fixes #58087.

A standard `type="kvcr"` secondary tier fails to initialize because `SecondaryTierFactory` passes `backpressure_detector=None` even when backpressure is not configured, while `KVCRSecondaryTierManager` does not accept that argument. Consequently, the server exits before it can serve a request.

Accept the optional detector in the KVCR constructor and forward it to `SecondaryTierManager`. Keep the parameter at the end of the existing signature to preserve existing positional arguments. Route the existing KVCR test helper through the production factory and exercise request/load behavior with both default and explicitly configured backpressure.

This restores the constructor contract introduced by [#50045](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50045) after the KVCR adapter landed in [#53624](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53624). Default configurations retain a `None` detector; explicitly configured detectors are preserved rather than silently discarded.

Duplicate checks on 2026-09-22 found no existing issue or PR addressing this constructor mismatch. [#57500](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57500) concerns buffer lifetime after a native startup failure and leaves this signature unchanged.

## Test Plan

Run the focused suites with the optional KVCR package installed:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="" .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_kvcr_tier.py \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_factory.py \
```

commits.pr_title: [UX] Skip checkpoint shards an MTP head does not load
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

MTP heads load from their target's checkpoint, so loaders that read whole files (InstantTensor, fastsafetensors, multi-thread, eager/prefetch) read the entire checkpoint a second time, only for the head's `load_weights` to drop almost all of it. This PR lets a model say which checkpoint weights it does not load, and `DefaultModelLoader` drops the safetensors shards that hold nothing else before any loader opens them.

Related: #58016 adds a similar model hook for per-tensor skipping in the lazy safetensors path (see Details).

## Claims

- With `--load-format instanttensor`, the MTP drafter no longer re-reads the target checkpoint: 704 G → 20 G on GLM-5.3, 149 G → 3.35 G on DeepSeek-V4-Flash, 61.3 G → 10.2 G on Nemotron-3.5-Lightning.
- Total model load time drops accordingly: 226.5 s → 127.5 s (GLM-5.3, TP=8), 56.5 s → 36.6 s (DeepSeek-V4-Flash, TP=2), 22.8 s → 14.9 s (Nemotron, 1 GPU).
- Generated text and draft acceptance are unchanged.
- Opted in: DeepSeek-V4 (NVIDIA), DeepSeek-V3.2 / GLM-5.2 / GLM-5.3 (NVIDIA and ROCm), Nemotron-H, Qwen3.5, Qwen3-Next MTP heads. Models without the hook are unaffected.

## Validation

End to end on 8x H200, local XFS, InstantTensor 0.2.0, one run per configuration:

```bash
vllm serve <model> --load-format instanttensor --max-model-len 4096 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":1}' [--tensor-parallel-size N]
```

| Model | Drafter read, before → after | Shards read | Drafter load | Total model load | Draft tokens accepted, before / after |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `zai-org/GLM-5.3`, TP=8 | 704 G → 20.0 G | 4 of 141 | 109.9 s → 3.4 s | 226.5 s → 127.5 s | 54 of 65 / 54 of 65 |
| `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash`, TP=2 | 149 G → 3.35 G | 1 of 46 | 25.7 s → 0.9 s | 56.5 s → 36.6 s | 60 of 60 / 60 of 60 |
| `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-BF16`, 1 GPU | 61.3 G → 10.2 G | 3 of 14 | 10.1 s → 2.2 s | 22.8 s → 14.9 s | 59 of 61 / 59 of 61 |

Acceptance is a smoke check from one 120-token greedy completion per run, not an accuracy evaluation; the completions matched before and after.

A separate-repo drafter is unaffected: `zai-org/GLM-5.3` with `RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-speculator.dspark` on this branch loads the 2.3 G speculator in 0.5 s (total 116.9 s) and generates correctly.

For each opted-in head, the new rule was compared with the original filtering on every weight name of a real checkpoint (GLM-5.2, GLM-5.2-FP8, DeepSeek-V4-Flash, DeepSeek-V4-Pro, Nemotron-3.5-Lightning, Qwen3.5-9B, Qwen3.5-27B): zero mismatches. Scanning the 141 GLM-5.3 shard headers takes 0.12 s.

Tests and linters:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_filter_duplicate_safetensors.py \
  tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_ep_weight_filter.py \
  tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_mm_encoder_only_weight_filter.py   # 51 passed
pre-commit run --files <changed files>                                      # passed
pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files <changed files>        # passed
```

Not validated:

- GLM-5.2 itself was not run end to end; GLM-5.3 uses the same `glm_moe_dsa` architecture and the same MTP head. From the published index, GLM-5.2 keeps 6 of 282 shards (29.9 of 1,403 GiB) and GLM-5.2-FP8 keeps 4 of 141 (20.0 of 704 GiB).
- The ROCm DeepSeek-V3.2 head has the same edit as the NVIDIA one but was not run on AMD hardware.
- Qwen3.5 and Qwen3-Next were not run end to end.
- Only InstantTensor was run end to end. The other safetensors load formats share the code path (the filter runs before the format is chosen) and are covered by the loader unit test only.

## Details

**Design.** A model may define `is_unused_checkpoint_weight(name) -> bool`, returning True for checkpoint weights it does not load. `DefaultModelLoader` passes it through a new `Source.is_unused_weight` field, and `filter_safetensors_files_by_weight_name` reads each shard's header and keeps only shards with at least one wanted tensor. Each opted-in head's `load_weights` calls the same rule, so the filter and the loader cannot drift apart. If the rule rejects every shard, the file list is left unchanged so the head's own missing-weight error still fires.

**Why shard level.** Whole-file loaders cannot skip single tensors, so the file list is the only lever vLLM has for them. MTP weights sit in a few shards, which is why this is enough.

**Relation to #58016 (not a duplicate).** #58016 adds an equivalent hook (`skip_checkpoint_weight`) and `Source` field but applies it per tensor inside `safetensors_weights_iterator`, which only helps the lazy safetensors path, and opts in only the DeepSeek-V4 DSpark drafter. This PR covers the whole-file loaders and the MTP heads. The two are complementary (drop shards, then skip tensors inside the kept ones), but the hooks are named differently, so whichever lands second should adopt the other's name and rebase the few shared lines in `default_loader.py`. Open PRs and issues were also searched for "MTP checkpoint load weights", "MTP shards skip", "draft model load entire checkpoint" and "MTP double load"; nothing else overlaps.

**Limitations.**

- Kept shards are still read in full. Qwen3.5 gains little: its head also loads `embed_tokens` and `lm_head`, which are spread across shards (Qwen3.5-27B keeps 5 of 11, Qwen3.5-9B keeps 4 of 4).
- Other MTP heads (DeepSeek V3, GLM-4, Kimi, Inkling, the ROCm/XPU V4 variants and others) are not opted in and behave as before.
- This does not help the EP weight filter under InstantTensor. On DeepSeek-V4-Flash, V4-Pro and Nemotron every shard holds at least one local expert at EP sizes 2, 4 and 8, so that needs per-tensor skipping inside InstantTensor itself.
- Loaders outside `DefaultModelLoader` (Run:ai streamer, tensorizer, sharded state, IPC weight cache) are untouched.
